1) FGFR inhibitor–associated serous retinopathy (FGFRi-associated retinopathy)
   - Rationale: bilateral symmetric yellow foveal lesions with hyperreflective/thickened ellipsoid/interdigitation zones on OCT, central hypoautofluorescence, no leakage on FA/ICG, progression to small foveal serous retinal detachments — pattern highly characteristic of FGFR-targeted therapy toxicity in a patient with FGFR2-amplified gastric cancer.

2) MEK/MAPK-pathway inhibitor–associated retinopathy (MEKAR)
   - Rationale: produces very similar bilateral serous detachments with minimal angiographic leakage and OCT changes; consider if patient received MAPK-pathway inhibitors instead of or in addition to FGFR inhibitors.

3) Paraneoplastic acute exudative polymorphous vitelliform maculopathy (AEPVM) / paraneoplastic vitelliform lesions
   - Rationale: can present with bilateral yellow subretinal/foveal lesions and serous detachments in patients with underlying carcinoma; imaging can be variable and may show limited leakage.

4) Central serous chorioretinopathy (CSC)
   - Rationale: can produce serous foveal detachments and RPE changes but typically shows focal leakage on FA/ICG and is often asymmetric; less likely given current angiographic absence of leakage.

5) Small/atypical choroidal metastases with overlying serous detachment
   - Rationale: systemic gastric adenocarcinoma can metastasize to the choroid; B-scan was reported normal and no mass was described, making this less likely but still important to consider.

Recommended immediate actions (for treating team / retina specialist):
- Urgently confirm current and recent systemic oncology treatments (specifically FGFR inhibitors and MAPK-pathway inhibitors) with the oncology record.
- Measure and document best-corrected visual acuity and perform repeat macular OCT (and OCT through follow-up) to quantify subretinal fluid.
- Discuss with oncology whether temporary dose hold or adjustment of any suspected offending agent is appropriate (do not stop systemic therapy without oncology agreement).
- If diagnosis uncertain, obtain multimodal imaging review by a retina specialist (color fundus photos, repeat FAF, repeat FA/ICG and OCT-A if needed) and consider electroretinography or paraneoplastic antibody testing if paraneoplastic process suspected.
